correctness.rationale: Soft-thresholding each leaf about hub h leaves a scalar hub KKT equation with clipped terms and strictly positive slope at least m_0; the unique solution yields fusion exactly when |h-y_i|≤λa_i/m_i. To check persistence at simultaneous events, scale by τ=1/λ and write v=τh and q_i=v-τy_i. On every incident affine clip-pattern cell with unsaturated set I, let M_I=m_0+Σ_{j∈I}m_j and S be the saturated signed penalty sum. At an upper contact q_i=c_i=a_i/m_i, the branch slope satisfies τM_I q_i'=M_Ic_i+S. If i is unsaturated then M_I≥m_0+m_i and S≥-Σ_{j≠i}a_j; if i is saturated then its sign is positive, S≥a_i-Σ_{j≠i}a_j and M_I≥m_0. Both bounds give q_i'≥0 by the local budget; at a lower contact the mirrored bounds give q_i'≤0. A branch identically on the boundary has slope zero. Thus no affine piece on the decreasing-τ side can leave the fused strip, including ties and simultaneous changes. For λ=0, the tied-to-hub leaves can form one fused block for small positive λ: all strictly unequal data stay outside the clipped strips, since |h-y_0|≤λΣa_j/m_0, and the tied block's drift divided by λ has magnitude at most Σ_{outside}a_j/M_I≤a_i/m_i for every tied leaf by its own budget. This handles initial exact ties. For failure on leaf i, take y_0=0, y_i=H>0 and the rest very large, so the other leaves stay above the hub on a chosen finite interval (use the same uniform bound on |h-y_0|). Writing B=Σ_{j≠i}a_j and c=(m_0+m_i)a_i/m_i<B, the fused KKT solution exists exactly for m_0H/(B+c)≤λ≤m_0H/(B-c) there. An interior test and a later test beyond the upper endpoint give actual fusion followed by separation. The stated four-leaf rational fits satisfy the clipping and hub equations. Q=BM^-1B^T has diagonal a_i²(1/m_0+1/m_i) and off-diagonal a_i a_j/m_0; its weak dominance inequality is exactly the local budget. Normalizing the weights to sum one changes this budget to a_i/Σa_j≥m_i/(m_0+2m_i); the sum condition is necessary and distributing any slack proves feasibility even at equality. This includes k=1 and the stated equal-mass examples. evidence: Tibshirani–Taylor eq. (23) provides weak diagonal dominance as a sufficient condition for dual boundary persistence. Their 1D discussion does not identify primal edge equality with dual interior on arbitrary graphs. Duan et al. supplies the primal sufficient implication independently. Hoefling gives a general max-flow split-event algorithm. Chiquet et al. give no-split complete pairwise penalty families, including weights depending on the data.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The max-flow method detects path events for provided data, but its stated conclusions do not furnish this uniform if-and-only-if classification or penalty-design obstruction. Data-dependent complete-pair families do not instantiate arbitrary fixed sparse star-spoke penalties.

evidence: In the full-rank lasso, eq. (9) gives signed slopes from the active inverse Gram. The sufficiency proof says zero entries remain zero as λ increases. The three-vertex path result covers k=2 exactly and constructs fusions followed by splitting; it does not extend to k≥3 stars by parameter substitution. The cycle has dependent edge rows, a different graph and different exact criteria; the fixed-λ star variation theorem has a different quantifier.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A converse can be derived using established lasso equations, but requires an actual construction. For example if row i fails, choose signs s with s_i=1 and (Qs)_i<0. Pick a target θ with θ_i=0 and other entries strictly of signs s, and realize center By=θ+λ_0Qs for λ_0>0. Above λ_0 the all-active solution θ+(λ_0-λ)Qs has that sign pattern locally; below λ_0 the KKT dual coordinate for i moves strictly inside [-1,1] while the other signs persist. This supports sharpness but is not a quoted converse of the earlier sufficient result. The frozen star proof additionally gives an explicit interval and observations directly on the star. The mass-feasibility algebra is not credited on its own.

evidence: For z=M^(1/2)u and D=BM^(-1/2), condition on θ=Dz and minimize over z. This gives 1/2(θ-By)^T Q^-1(θ-By)+λ||θ||_1. Q=DD^T is positive definite by row rank. The whitened ordinary lasso has inverse Gram Q, every center By is attainable, and θ_i=0 is exactly primal edge fusion. Duan et al. Lemma 2 gives precisely this reduction in general form and Theorem 1's proof gives weak-DD primal shrinkage. The same-day two-input star variation theorem yields the same inequality when its measuring weights are chosen equal to the penalties, with the same resulting algebra for choosing weights.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The reduction identifies genuine sufficient coverage. The earlier stated lasso theorem is one-way, not a universal no-dropout converse. Starting with a bad sign direction, one must still realize it by data and establish a loss of support as λ decreases (equivalently, unfusion as λ increases), not just show an adverse slope on an abstract face. Efron's strict positive cone and Duan's weak version are not cited as necessary for a given data path. The two-input result compares different data with fixed λ, not zero support along a single data path as λ varies.

originality.rationale: A stronger prior sufficient result than the frozen citation alone was identified: Duan et al. already give primal coordinatewise shrinkage after the exact full-row-rank TV-to-lasso reduction under weak diagonal dominance. The sufficiency and its algebraic rewriting are not new. The surviving content is the sharp necessity for universal persistence with a genuine positive-length fusion-then-separation witness for any failed star row, and the resulting penalty-design feasibility for this path property. Same-day weighted-path and star-variation records overlap substantively but do not state that surviving result for branching stars. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A general all-response weak positive-cone/no-dropout converse, or an earlier star/weighted-tree classification, could fully subsume this classification. It was not established by the inspected primary sources. No priority order is inferred for distinct same-day entries.

value.rationale: An exact obstruction determines whether an irreversible-merge rule is universally sound on the fundamental branching graph and whether any positive edge-weight design can make it so. The converse supplies actual splitting after a nondegenerate interval, not merely a failed certificate, and the equal-mass four-spoke obstruction shows that tuning all the penalties cannot always fix it. The known sufficient criterion and the mass algebra alone are not the contribution. No general graph or statistical risk claim is made.
